pl-l4d12c6-d1e115.summary: States that this sacrament was instituted for two reasons: for the increase of virtue, that is of charity, and as medicine for daily weakness.
claims: The eucharist increases charity and heals daily weakness.

pl-l4d12c6-d1e118.summary: Quotes Ambrose: if whenever Christ's blood is poured out it is poured for the remission of sins, I who always sin should always receive it and always have the medicine.
claims: The eucharist is constant medicine for constant sin.

pl-l4d12c6-d1e127.summary: Quotes Augustine: this offering is repeated daily, though Christ suffered once, because we sin daily with sins without which mortal weakness cannot live; since we fall daily, Christ is daily mystically immolated for us. He gave this sacrament so that, since we sin daily and he can no longer die, we obtain remission through it. He is daily eaten and drunk in truth but remains whole and living.
claims: The daily offering answers daily sin.
Christ is eaten in truth and remains whole.

pl-l4d12c6-d1e140.summary: Adds Augustine: it is called a mystery of faith because you must believe that our salvation consists in it.
claims: Our salvation is to be believed to consist in it.

pl-l4d12c6-d1e146.summary: Answers whether one should communicate daily with Augustine: I neither praise nor blame receiving the eucharist daily, but I urge communion every Sunday. If the mind is set on sinning, it is burdened rather than purified by receiving; one stung by sin who has no will to sin further and makes satisfaction with tears and prayers may approach securely, if not weighed down by mortal sins.
claims: Daily communion is neither praised nor blamed; Sunday communion is urged.
A mind set on sin is burdened by receiving.
Those free of mortal sin who repent may approach securely.

pl-l4d12c6-d1e155.summary: Adds the rule that, if not more often, people should communicate at least three times a year, at Easter, Pentecost, and Christmas, unless prevented by crimes; all who do not wish to be cut off from the Church should communicate.
claims: The faithful must communicate at least at Easter, Pentecost, and Christmas.

pl-l4d12c6.summary: States that the sacrament was instituted for two reasons: the increase of virtue, charity, and medicine for daily weakness. Ambrose and Augustine: as we sin daily, we should receive daily the medicine of Christ's blood, mystically immolated for us daily, and he is eaten and drunk in truth yet remains whole and living. On frequency, Augustine neither praises nor blames daily communion but urges it on Sundays, warning that a mind set on sin is burdened rather than cleansed, while one without mortal sin who repents of daily faults may approach securely. The faithful should communicate at least three times a year, at Easter, Pentecost, and Christmas.
claims: The eucharist was instituted to increase charity and heal daily weakness.
It is a remedy for daily sins.
Augustine neither praises nor blames daily communion, but urges it on Sundays.
Those set on sin are burdened, not cleansed, by it.
The faithful must communicate at least three times a year.
